summary: A ready CPU expert tier: one layer's CPU-computed routed experts in the integer block order (the device's bits), split over a pinned worker pool, served from a host-work-mailbox payload
implementation_scope: C++20 ExpertPool (one thread per physical core minus the caller's, pinned on Linux; flat batches with epoch-tagged lock-free claims; spin then sleep) and HostExpertTier (an expert table over bundles read in place, routes grouped by expert in chunks of up to 8 tokens, gate/up rows with the declared SwiGLU and intermediate quantization in one pooled phase, down rows, per-row posts, FP32 inputs quantized per route by each expert's declared quantizer, unweighted per-route rows), the mailbox payloads and crit_tier_serve, a C interface for ctypes; the experts slot's device form on the CPU (cpu_tier.py, bundles.py) over the native tier or host-expert-arithmetic's torch declared order. The device's post and join live in heterogeneous-expert-dispatch.

agent_guidance.use_when: Experts do not all fit on the device and crit eval probe's CPU expert lane, alone or beside the link, beats copying misses over the link (recon's placement prints both); start candidate 1 on it there
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Every expert fits on the device, or the probed lane and a measured layer give the CPU no share on the target machine
provides: ExpertPool: one worker per physical core minus the caller's, pinned, flat batches claimed with one compare-and-swap of an epoch-tagged word, spin then yield then sleep, a task's exception rethrown after the batch drains

HostExpertTier::compute: a layer's CPU routes, each expert's rows read once for all of its tokens (up to 8 a chunk), rows split over the pool, bitwise equal to a serial computation for any pool size, ISA or store layout
The expert composition declared end to end: host_int's integer rows, swiglu_declared and the intermediate's declared quantizer (E2M1 x 2 or INT8), so the device's kernels give the same bits
A host-work-mailbox payload of FP32 token rows (route keys and tokens, the rows, room for the outputs: input_layout) and crit_tier_serve, the mailbox handler that serves it
interleave_matrix for the CPU's store layout, and telemetry: routes, expert chunks, ms per phase, expert bytes read
engine_supplies: The experts in pinned host memory (interleaved for the CPU; the device cache's store beside it) with their scale decoders and post factors
A device kernel that quantizes the layer's input as the tier expects, writes the payload, posts and joins (poll join from measure_joins), and sums the rows with routing weights in plan order
The CPU share: device-expert-cache admission limits from split.py, fed with this tier's measured layer times and the link's
preserve: One declared arithmetic on every processor: integer block rows, swiglu_declared, the declared quantizer
Per-route unweighted rows, summed on the device in plan order, never a host-side sum over experts
A core left to the caller (the host loop and the mailbox's service thread); the CPU share from measurement on the target
adapt: Rows per task, worker count, pinning and the payload's route capacity
Expert composition (activation, fused or separate gate/up) as long as the device declares the same

code_files.purpose: Epoch-tagged claims, pinning from sysfs, spin/yield/sleep parking
TierExpert, TierBatch, HostExpertTier, the payload layout, interleave_matrix, TierStats
Routes grouped by expert, the three pooled phases, the payload server
Python model of the pool's epoch-tagged claim, the tier's chunking and the device's plan-order sum
A C interface over the tier and its pool, and crit_tier_serve, the host-work-mailbox handler
The experts slot's nvfp4 / int4 bundle layout and pack, read in place by the tier
CpuTier: the expert table over bundles, the native tier or the torch declared order, the mailbox handler's address and payload layout

requires.hardware: Any CPU host-expert-arithmetic's integer rows run on (AVX-512 VNNI and AVX2 fast paths on x86, scalar elsewhere); a GPU and mapped pinned memory for the mailbox wiring
requires.model: Expert-routed models with 4-bit block-scaled experts (NVFP4 or INT4) and a SwiGLU expert
requires.workload: Decode and verify rounds whose expert misses measured dispatch gives the CPU

contract.input: TierExperts sharing [2 * inter][hidden] and [hidden][inter] (an expert table filled by set_expert, views of bundles the engine keeps), an ExpertPool, and per call a TierBatch (quantized inputs), an InputBatch (FP32 token rows) or a mailbox payload of FP32 rows
contract.output: Each route's unweighted expert output row in FP32, bitwise equal to the declared arithmetic computed serially
contract.ownership: Views only: the engine owns the experts, the payload and the outputs; the pool's threads live with the pool
contract.failure: Mismatched expert shapes, an unsupported ISA, a bad batch geometry or an expert id out of range throw std::invalid_argument; a task's exception is rethrown by the pool after its batch drains
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; engines own the pool and the tier beside their mailbox

validation.host: crit_host_expert_tier_tests: a layer of 21 routes over 6 experts equals a serial computation bit for bit for pools of 0, 2 and 5 workers, scalar and the fastest ISA, both store layouts and both intermediate formats; per-row posts and FP32 inputs over 36 configurations; both payloads serve the same bits; 3,000 pools started and stopped, 253,500 batches, each task once in its own batch. Plugin tests: the device form is the declared order per route summed by FMAs in route order, the native tier and the torch path give the same bits, a token alone gives its batched bits, a bundle store read in place equals loaded experts, within the quantization's error of the dense FP64 block
validation.native: Built and run on a Ryzen 5 9600 under WSL2 with GCC (AVX-512 VNNI path); the native tier equals the int-block-experts device kernels bit for bit on an RTX 5090 at hidden 2560 / inter 640 for 1, 3 and 8 tokens, on random experts and on real NVFP4 checkpoint experts
validation.performance: Ryzen 5 9600, 6 threads, 2.76 MB experts (hidden 2560, inter 640), 6 experts a layer: 0.58 / 0.77 / 0.89 ms a layer at 1 / 2 / 3 tokens an expert, 30 / 23 / 20 GB/s of experts
